about: Twelve made-up client situations for designing and testing Challenge 2. No scenario describes a real person. The first four follow the needs IHH named: shelter, microloans, travel to reunify with family, and job help.
how_to_use: Use them however helps. The right services depend on the directory you use and must be checked on the day.

scenarios.title: A bed after recuperative care
scenarios.client: Ray, 62. Leaves recuperative care in five days. Walks with a walker. Has Medi-Cal. Lost his ID. Last had an address in Santa Ana.
scenarios.in_their_words: They say I'm done here Friday. I can't go back under the bridge with this leg. Where do I go?
constraints: Uses a walker; needs a lower bunk or accessible site
Basic phone, calls and texts only

scenarios.title: A small loan to start working again
scenarios.client: Marisol, 41. Sold food at swap meets before she lost her housing. Wants to restart. Speaks Spanish, some English. Has a phone with data.
scenarios.in_their_words: Yo sé trabajar. Solo necesito como dos mil dólares para el equipo y el permiso.
constraints: Does not want to share anything about immigration status

scenarios.title: Getting home to family
scenarios.client: Devon, 29. His sister in Phoenix has said he can live with her. He has an ID and no money for the trip.
scenarios.in_their_words: My sister said come. I just can't get there.
constraints: Wants to leave within two weeks

scenarios.title: Back to work
scenarios.client: Tanya, 35. Drove a forklift for six years. Two-year gap. Has a phone. Mentions an old conviction in passing.
scenarios.in_their_words: I can work. I just don't know how to explain the last two years, and I've got nothing to wear to an interview.

scenarios.title: No ID, no birth certificate
scenarios.client: Walt, 54. Wallet stolen. Born in Texas. Needs ID to apply for almost anything.
scenarios.in_their_words: Everything asks for ID. I can't get ID without my birth certificate, and I can't get that without ID.

scenarios.title: No income at 67
scenarios.client: Gloria, 67. No income. Hard of hearing. Not sure what she qualifies for.
scenarios.in_their_words: I don't hear well on the phone. Is there somebody I can go see?
constraints: Phone calls are hard; prefers in person or text

scenarios.title: Getting around
scenarios.client: Andre, 48. Has a clinic visit and two job interviews this month. No car.
scenarios.in_their_words: I can get the job if I can get there.

scenarios.title: Twenty-three and no phone
scenarios.client: Jas, 23. Lost their phone. Aged out of foster care. Staying on friends' couches until last week.
scenarios.in_their_words: I can't do anything without a phone. I don't even know what's out there for people my age.

scenarios.title: A veteran who never used the VA
scenarios.client: Hank, 59. Served in the Army in the 1980s. Not sure about his discharge papers. Never signed up for VA care.
scenarios.in_their_words: I never asked them for anything. Don't know if I even count.

scenarios.title: Not safe to go back
scenarios.client: Lena, 38. Says she cannot return to where she was staying.
scenarios.in_their_words: I can't go back there. He'll find me.
constraints: May be using a shared device

scenarios.title: A medical question in the wrong place
scenarios.in_their_words: These water pills make me dizzy. Can I just stop taking them?

scenarios.title: The listing might be out of date
scenarios.client: Sam, 44. Heard about a program from someone at a shelter and wants to know if it is still running.
scenarios.in_their_words: A guy told me there's a place that helps with deposits. Is that real?
constraints: Only has the name he was told, possibly wrong
